definitions.explanation: A film that records and presents real events, people, or topics rather than telling a fictional story.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}の{記録映画|きろくえいが}を{観|み}た。
この{記録映画|きろくえいが}は{自然|しぜん}の{美|うつく}しさを{見事|みごと}にとらえている。
examples.english: This documentary beautifully captures the beauty of nature.

examples.japanese: {被災地|ひさいち}の{復興|ふっこう}をテーマにした{記録映画|きろくえいが}が{映画祭|えいがさい}で{上映|じょうえい}された。
examples.english: A documentary about the recovery of the disaster-affected area was screened at the film festival.

notes:
The traditional Japanese term for documentary film, composed of {記録|きろく} (record, documentation) and {映画|えいが} (movie, film). While ドキュメンタリー (the loanword) is also widely used in modern Japanese, {記録映画|きろくえいが} remains the standard native term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記録映画|きろくえいが}を{撮|と}る — to shoot a documentary
- {記録映画|きろくえいが}を{制作|せいさく}する — to produce a documentary
- {記録映画|きろくえいが}{監督|かんとく} — documentary filmmaker
- {記録映画|きろくえいが}{祭|さい} — documentary film festival

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ドキュメンタリー — documentary (loanword; more common in casual speech and TV)
- {劇映画|げきえいが} — feature film, narrative film (fictional; the counterpart)
- {娯楽映画|ごらくえいが} — entertainment film (focuses on commercial appeal)

USAGE:
{記録映画|きろくえいが} tends to sound more formal or traditional than ドキュメンタリー. It is preferred in academic writing, film criticism, and historical contexts.
